children.text: oṃ bhūs tat savituḥ śaṃ no devīḥ śāntā dyauḥ śaṃ na indrāgnī śaṃ no vāto vātu uṣā apa svasus tama iti śāntigaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. [The hymns beginning] “Earth,” “That of <s>Savitṛ</s>,” “May the divine ones favor us,” “Peaceful is heaven,” “May <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> favor us,” “May the wind blow favorably for us,” “Dawn,” and “Drive away your sister's darkness” constitute the <s>śānti</s> (pacification) group.

children.text: kṛtyāpratiharaṇo dūṣyā dūṣir asi īśānāṃ tvā samaṃ jyotir uto asy abandhukṛd ye purastāt suparṇas tvā yāṃ te cakruḥ pratīcīnaphalo yad duṣkṛtam ayaṃ pratisaro yāṃ kalpayantīti kṛtyāpratiharaṇāni
children.translated_text: For counteracting sorcery there are [the formulas beginning] “By the corruptible,” “You are a corrupter,” “You among the rulers,” “Equal light,” “And he is one who makes [people] kinless,” “Those who are in front,” “The fair-winged one [takes] you,” “The [spell] that they made against you,” “Bearing fruit backward,” “Whatever evil has been done,” “This is the counter-charm,” and “The [spell] which they prepare.” These are the formulas for counteracting sorcery.

children.text: iti kṛtyāgaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sorcery group.

children.text: cātanaḥ stuvānam idaṃ havir ye 'māvāsyām upa prāgān niḥsālām arāyakṣayaṇaṃ śaṃ no devī pṛśniparṇy ā paśyati tānt satyaujās tvayā pūrvaṃ purastād yukto antardāve juhuta prāgnaye rakṣohaṇam ity anuvākaś cātanāni
children.translated_text: For expulsion there are [the formulas beginning] “The one who praises,” “This oblation,” “Those who on the new-moon night,” “He has approached,” “Out of the hall,” “The destruction of the niggardly demon,” “May the divine one favor us,” “The <s>pṛśniparṇī</s> (speckled-leaf plant),” “He sees,” “Those [foes], O you of true strength,” “Before [others], through you,” “Harnessed in front,” “Offer within the forest fire,” “For <s>Agni</s>,” and “Demon-slaying.” This <s>anuvāka</s> (section) comprises the expulsion formulas.

children.text: iti cātanagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the expulsion group.

children.text: mātṛnāmā divyo gandharva ā paśyatīmaṃ me agne yau te māteti mātṛnāmāni
children.translated_text: The formulas naming the Mothers are [those beginning] “The heavenly <s>Gandharva</s>,” “He sees,” “This [prayer] of mine, O <s>Agni</s>,” and “Those two mothers of yours.”

children.text: iti mātṛgaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the group concerning the Mothers.

children.text: vāstoṣpatīya āśānām āśāpālebhya ihaiva dhruvām ṛdhaṅmantro yonim uta putraḥ pitaram indrasya gṛho 'sīti catasro dive svāhāśamavarma me pṛthivyai śrotrāyeti dhanvānīti dve ūrjaṃ bibhrad iti ṣaṭsatyaṃ bṛhad ity anuvāko vāstoṣpatīyāni
children.translated_text: The formulas concerning the Lord of the Dwelling are [those beginning] “Of the quarters,” “To the guardians of the quarters,” “Right here,” “The firm one,” “The prospering formula [to] the womb,” “And the son [approaches] the father,” and “You are the house of <s>Indra</s>”; also four [verses beginning] “To heaven, svāhā,” “May my armor [bring] welfare,” and “For earth, for hearing”; two called “Bearing a bow”; six beginning “Bearing nourishment”; and the <s>anuvāka</s> beginning “Great truth.”

children.text: iti vāstugaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the dwelling group.

children.text: pāpmahā vi devā jarasāvṛtam apa naḥ śośucad agham ava mā pāpmann iti pāpmahā
children.translated_text: The destroyers of evil are [the formulas beginning] “Apart, O gods,” “Enveloped by old age,” “May the burning evil go away from us,” and “Protect me, O evil.”

children.text: iti pāpmahā gaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the evil-destroying group.

children.text: takmanāśano jarāyujaḥ prathamo yad agnir ud agātāṃ daśavṛkṣa muñca kṣetriyāt tvā hariṇasya raghuṣyado muñcāmi tvā bhavāśarvau manve vāṃ yo giriṣu dive svāhāgnis takmānam agner ivāsyāva mā pāpmant sṛjāva jyām iva varaṇo vārayātā imaṃ yavaṃ vidradhasya balāsasya namo rūrāyeti dve śīrṣaktiṃ śīrṣāmayam iti takmanāśanāni
children.translated_text: The fever-destroying formulas are [those beginning] “The first, born from the womb,” “When <s>Agni</s> rose,” “The ten-tree,” “Release you from inherited disease,” “Of the swift-running antelope,” “I release you,” “O <s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s>, I call upon you both,” “He who is in the mountains,” “To heaven, svāhā,” “<s>Agni</s> [drives away] fever,” “As from <s>Agni</s>,” “Release this evil from me like a bowstring,” “May <s>Varaṇa</s> ward it off,” “This barley,” “Of the abscess,” “Of consumption,” two beginning “Homage to <s>Rūra</s>,” and “Headache and pain of the head.”

children.text: iti takmanāśanagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fever-destroying group.

children.text: duḥsvapnanāśanāni dauṣvapnyaṃ daurjīvityaṃ paro 'paihi yo na jīvo 'si pary āvarte duṣvapnyād yat svapne annam aśnami yo na stāyad dipsati yo naḥ suptāṃ jāgrato yan me manso duṣvapnyaṃ kāma svapnaṃ suptvā vidma te svapneti trayaḥ paryāyā duḥsvapnanāśanāni
children.translated_text: The nightmare-destroying formulas are [those beginning] “Bad dreaming and wretched living,” “Go far away,” “You who are not alive,” “I turn away from the nightmare,” “When in a dream I eat food,” “He who seeks to steal from us,” “That which [comes] to us sleeping from one who is awake,” “The nightmare arising from my mind,” “O desire, the dream,” “Having slept,” and “We know you, O dream.” These three cycles are the nightmare-destroying formulas.

children.text: iti duḥsvapnanāśanagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the nightmare-destroying group.

children.text: āyuṣyo yathā dyauḥ prāṇāpānāv ojo 'si tubhyam evākṣībhyāṃ te muñcāmi tvota devā āvatas ta upa priyam antakāya mṛtyava ā rabhasva prāṇāya namo viṣāsahim ity āyuṣyāṇi
children.translated_text: The formulas for long life are [those beginning] “As heaven,” “The in-breath and out-breath,” “You are vigor,” “For you alone,” “From your two eyes,” “I release you,” “The gods [protect] you,” “Those protections of yours,” “Near the beloved,” “For <s>Antaka</s>, for <s>Mṛtyu</s>,” “Take hold,” “Homage to the life-breath,” and “The poison-conquering one.”

children.text: iti āyuṣyagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the longevity group.

children.text: varcasyo ye triṣaptā asmin vasu prātar agniṃ hastivarcasaṃ siṃhe vyāghre yaśo havir yaśasaṃ mendro girāv aragarāṭeṣu yathā somaḥ prātaḥsavane yac ca varco akṣeṣu yena mahānaghnyā jaghanam iti varcasyāni
children.translated_text: The formulas for brilliance are [those beginning] “Those three sevens,” “Wealth in this [person],” “<s>Agni</s> in the morning,” “Possessing an elephant's splendor,” “In the lion and the tiger,” “The oblation of fame,” “May <s>Indra</s> [grant] me fame,” “On the mountain, among the aragarāṭas,” “As <s>Soma</s> at the morning pressing,” “And whatever brilliance is in the dice,” and “That by which the great inviolable cow [has] her hind part.”

children.text: iti varcasyagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the brilliance group.

children.text: svastyayano amūḥ pāre pātaṃ na indrāpūṣaṇā tvaṣṭā me daivyaṃ yena soma namo devavadhebhyo 'bhayaṃ mitrāvaruṇāv upa prāgāt sahasrākṣo 'namitraṃ no adharād yamomṛtyur bṛhaspatir naḥ pari pātu tyam ū ṣu trātāram indraḥ sutrāmā sa sutrāmā ā mandrair indra marmāṇi te varma me dyāvāpṛthivī aindrāgnaṃ varma girayas te yat te madhyaṃ yās te prācīr mā naḥ paścād iti svastyayanāni
children.translated_text: The formulas for welfare and safe passage are [those beginning] “Those [women] on the farther shore,” “Protect us, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>,” “May <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> [grant] me the divine [protection],” “By which, O <s>Soma</s>,” “Homage to the divine weapons,” “Fearlessness, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>,” “The thousand-eyed one has approached,” “Let what is hostile be beneath us,” “<s>Yama</s> and <s>Mṛtyu</s>,” “May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> protect us on every side,” “That well-known protector,” “<s>Indra</s> the good protector,” “He is a good protector,” “With the gladdening [hymns], O <s>Indra</s>,” “Your vital points,” “May <s>Heaven-and-Earth</s> be my armor,” “The armor of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>,” “The mountains are yours,” “What is your middle,” “Those of yours that face east,” and “Do not [harm] us from behind.”

children.text: iti svastyayanagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the group for welfare and safe passage.

children.text: abhayaḥ svastidā viśāṃ brāhmaṇena paryuktāsi na tā arvā reṇukakāṭo abhayaṃ mitrāvaruṇāv abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī asmai grāmāya hataṃ tardaṃ pūṣemā āśā indraḥ sutrāmā maitaṃ panthāṃ svastidā viśāṃ patir nama te ghoṣiṇībhya ā te rāṣṭram idam uc chreyo yata indra bhayāmaha ity abhayāni
children.translated_text: The formulas for fearlessness are [those beginning] “The giver of welfare to the peoples,” “You are encompassed by a brahmin,” “Not those nearby,” “Reṇukakāṭa,” “Fearlessness, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>,” “Fearlessness, O <s>Heaven-and-Earth</s>,” “For this village,” “Strike the borer,” “May <s>Pūṣan</s> [guard] these quarters,” “<s>Indra</s> the good protector,” “Do not [follow] this path,” “The lord who gives welfare to the peoples,” “Homage to your clamorous [weapons],” “Your kingdom [comes] to you,” “This is better,” and “That of which, O <s>Indra</s>, we are afraid.”

children.text: ity abhayagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fearlessness group.

children.text: aparājito vidmā śarasya mā no cidann adārasṛt svastidā saṃśitaṃ me tvayā manyo yas te manyo etā devasenā avamanyur nirhastaḥ pari vartmāny abhibhūr indro jāyaty abhi tvendrety aparājitāni
children.translated_text: The invincibility formulas are [those beginning] “We know the arrow's [power],” “May it not cut us,” “The giver of welfare,” “My [weapon] is sharpened,” “Through you, O <s>Manyu</s>,” “That [power] of yours, O <s>Manyu</s>,” “These divine armies,” “Let hostile wrath be disarmed,” “Around the paths,” “<s>Indra</s> is born overpowering,” and “Against you, O <s>Indra</s>.”

children.text: ity aparājitagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the invincibility group.

children.text: śarmavarmā yaḥ sapatna itaś ca yad amutaś cāpendra dviṣato yūyaṃ naḥ pravata imam agna āyuṣe tisro devīr uruvyacā no indrasya śarmāsīti uttamāṃ varjayitvā yena devā asurāṇām anaḍudbhyas tvam iti dve tanūṣ ṭe vājin vājasya nu prasave devānāṃ patnīr adhi brūhi rakṣohaṇaṃ vājinaṃ ye srāktyaṃ varma me dyāvāpṛṭhivī aindrāgnaṃ varma bahulaṃ varma mahyam ayaṃ mitraḥ pṛthivyod akrāmad aspatnaṃ purastād iti śarmavarmā
children.translated_text: The shelter-and-armor formulas are [those beginning] “Whatever rival [is here],” “Both what is here and what is over there,” “Drive away the haters, O <s>Indra</s>,” “Do you lead us onward,” “This [offering], O <s>Agni</s>, for long life,” “The three goddesses,” “May the far-ranging one [protect] us,” and “You are <s>Indra</s>'s shelter,” excluding the last; also [the formulas beginning] “By which the gods [defeated] the Asuras,” two beginning “You [belong] to the oxen,” “Your body, O courser,” “Now at the impulse of strength,” “Address the wives of the gods,” “Demon-slaying,” “The courser,” “Those with twisted necklaces,” “May <s>Heaven-and-Earth</s> be my armor,” “The armor of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>,” “Abundant armor for me,” “This <s>Mitra</s>,” “He has risen from the earth,” and “Without a rival in front.” These are the shelter-and-armor formulas.

children.text: iti śarmavarmā gaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the shelter-and-armor group.

children.text: devapurā ye purastād brahma jajñānaṃ sahasradhāra evāgnir mā pātu agniṃ te vasuvantaṃ mitraḥ pṛthivyod akrāmad apa ny adhuḥ pauruṣeyaṃ vadhaṃ jitam asmākam iti devapurīyaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Devapurīya</s> group consists of the hymns beginning “Those divine strongholds which are in front,” “The <s>brahman</s> was born,” “The thousand-streamed one,” “May <s>Agni</s> protect me,” “For you, <s>Agni</s> attended by the <s>Vasus</s>,” “<s>Mitra</s> stepped up from the earth,” “They set it down beneath,” “The humanly inflicted blow,” and “Victory is ours.”

children.text: iti devapurīyagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Devapurīya</s> group.

children.text: rudro ye 'syāṃ prācī dig itirudragaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The hymns beginning “<s>Rudra</s>” and “Those who are in this eastern quarter” constitute the <s>Rudra</s> group.

children.text: iti rudragaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Rudra</s> group.

children.text: raudro rudra jalāṣabheṣaja ye 'syāṃ prācī dig ud itas trayo akraman bhavāśarvau manve vāṃ brahma jajñānam anāptā ye sahasradhāra eva grīṣmo hemanto anaḍudbhyas tvaṃ mahyam āpo vaiśvānaro yamo mṛtyur yāṃ te rudra yo agnau rudro bhavāśarvau mṛḍataṃ bhavāśarvāv idaṃ brūmo yas te sarpo vṛścikas tasmai prācyā diśo antardeśād iti raudragaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Raudra</s> group consists of the hymns beginning “The Raudra hymn,” “<s>Rudra</s>, whose medicine is soothing,” “Those who are in this eastern quarter,” “Up from here the three strode,” “<s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s>, I address you both,” “The <s>brahman</s> was born,” “Those who have not attained,” “The thousand-streamed one,” “Summer and winter,” “For the oxen,” “You waters, for me,” “<s>Vaiśvānara</s>,” “<s>Yama</s>, death,” “That which is yours, <s>Rudra</s>,” “The <s>Rudra</s> who is in <s>Agni</s>,” “<s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s>, be gracious,” “To <s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s> we say this,” “Whatever serpent or scorpion is yours,” and “For him, from the intermediate region of the eastern quarter.”

children.text: iti raudragaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Raudra</s> group.

children.text: citrāgaṇo mā no vidann adārasṛt svastidā viśām amūhoāre aghadviṣṭā agne yat te tapa iti pañca sūktāni rudra jalāṣabheṣaja ye 'syāṃ prācī dig vi devā uta devā agner manva itiprabhṛtīni mṛgārasūktāny uttamaṃ varjayitvāpa naḥ śośucad aghaṃ pṛthivyām agnaye mamāgne vrahma jajñānam anāptā ye sahasradhāre savitā prasavānāṃ nava prāṇān pātaṃ nas tvaṣṭā me yena soma namo devavadhebhyo 'bhayaṃ mitrāvaruṇāv upa prāgāt sahasrākṣaḥ siṃhe vyāghre 'bhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī grīṣmo hemanto 'naḍudbhyas tvaṃ mahyam āpo vaiśvānaro yamo mṛtyur abhi tvendra viśvajit trāyamāṇāyai imaṃ me agne viṣāṇā pāśān śakadhūmaṃ somārudreti dve bṛhaspatir nas tyam ū ṣu trātāram indraḥ sutrāmā ā mandrair indra marmāṇi te antakāya mṛtyavā ā rabhasvāyaṃ pratisaro 'yaṃ me varaṇo bhavāśarvau mṛḍataṃ prāṇāya namo 'gniṃ brūma ity arthasūktaṃ satyaṃ bṛhad iti dve prathame girayas te yat te madhyaṃ yās te prācīr mā naḥ paścād grīṣmas te bhūme varṣāṇy upasthās te bhūme mātaḥ sahasraśṛṅgo vṛṣabho jātavedā mā pra gāma patho yo yajñasya tasmai prācyā diśo antardeśād iti paryāyaś citrāgaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Citrā</s> group is the following sequence: the five hymns beginning mā no vidan, adārasṛt, svastidā viśām, amūho āre aghadviṣṭā, and “<s>Agni</s>, that heat of yours”; “<s>Rudra</s>, whose medicine is soothing”; “Those who are in this eastern quarter”; the <s>Mṛgāra</s> hymns beginning vi devā, uta devā, and agner manve, with the last omitted; and the hymns beginning apa naḥ śośucad agham, pṛthivyām, agnaye, mamāgne, brahma jajñānam, anāptā ye, sahasradhāre, savitā prasavānām, nava prāṇān, pātaṃ nas, tvaṣṭā me, yena soma, namo devavadhebhyaḥ, abhayaṃ mitrāvaruṇau, upa prāgāt sahasrākṣaḥ, siṃhe vyāghre, abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī, grīṣmo hemantaḥ, anaḍudbhyaḥ, tvaṃ mahyam āpaḥ, vaiśvānaraḥ, yamo mṛtyuḥ, abhi tvendra viśvajit, trāyamāṇāyai, imaṃ me agne, viṣāṇā pāśān, śakadhūmam, somārudra—the last two as a pair—bṛhaspatir naḥ, tyam ū ṣu trātāram, indraḥ sutrāmā, ā mandrair indra, marmāṇi te, antakāya mṛtyave, ā rabhasva, ayaṃ pratisaraḥ, ayaṃ me varaṇaḥ, bhavāśarvau mṛḍatam, prāṇāya namaḥ, agniṃ brūmaḥ (the <s>Arthasūkta</s>), satyaṃ bṛhat—the first two—girayas te, yat te madhyam, yās te prācīḥ, mā naḥ paścāt, grīṣmas te bhūme, varṣāṇi, upasthās te bhūme, mātaḥ, sahasraśṛṅgo vṛṣabhaḥ, jātavedā, mā pra gāma pathaḥ, yo yajñasya, and tasmai prācyā diśo antardeśāt. This complete sequence is the <s>Citrā</s> group.

children.text: iti citrāgaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Citrā</s> group.

children.text: patnīvanto aditir dyauḥ sinīvāli kuhūṃ devīm iti trīṇi sūktāni patnīvantaḥ
children.translated_text: The three hymns beginning “Accompanied by their wives,” “<s>Aditi</s> is heaven,” and “The goddesses <s>Sinīvālī</s> and <s>Kuhū</s>” constitute the <s>Patnīvanta</s> group.

children.text: iti patnīvantagaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Patnīvanta</s> group.

children.text: svasti mātra indra juṣasvāyā viṣṭhā śive te stāṃ pādābhyāṃ te saṃ te śirṣṇo vatso virāja ity ekā uccā patantam iti dve bhūyān indro viṣāsahiṃ sahamānam ity ādityagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hymns beginning svasti mātra, “<s>Indra</s>, accept,” āyā viṣṭhā, “May they be auspicious for you,” pādābhyāṃ te, saṃ te śīrṣṇaḥ, “The calf of <s>Virāj</s>” (one hymn), “Flying aloft” (two hymns), “Greater is <s>Indra</s>,” viṣāsahim, and sahamānam constitute the <s>Āditya</s> group.

children.text: śaṃ no devī śaṃ na indrāgnī śaṃ no vāto vātu śāntā dyauḥ pippalādiśāntigaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The hymns beginning “May the goddess grant us welfare,” “May <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> grant us welfare,” “May the wind blow welfare to us,” and “Heaven is pacified” constitute the <s>Pippalādiśānti</s> group.

children.text: iti pippalādiśāntigaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Pippalādiśānti</s> group.

children.text: gane yad iti pañca sūktāni pañcāpatyāni bhavanti pāñcajanyāni bhavanti pāñcāpatyo gaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The five hymns beginning gane yad are called the five <s>Apatya</s> hymns and the five <s>Janya</s> hymns; this is the <s>Pañcāpatya</s> group.

children.text: iti pañcāpatyagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Pañcāpatya</s> group.

children.text: ambayo yanti śambhumayobhubhyāṃ brahma jajñānam asya vāmasya yo rohita ud asya krtavo mūrdhāham iti dve sūkte viṣāsahim iti salilagaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The hymns beginning ambayo yanti, “For welfare and happiness,” “The <s>brahman</s> was born,” “Of this gracious one,” “The one who is red,” “Up rise his rays,” mūrdhāham (two hymns), and viṣāsahim constitute the <s>Salila</s> group.

children.text: iti salilagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Salila</s> group.

children.text: ye triṣaptā iti viśvakarmā gaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hymn beginning “Those three times seven” constitutes the <s>Viśvakarman</s> group.

children.text: aghadviṣṭā devajātā śaṃ no devī varaṇo vārayātai pippalī vidradhasya yā babhrava iti gaṇakarmā gaṇo bhaisajyaś ca bhavati
children.translated_text: The hymns beginning aghadviṣṭā, devajātā, “May the goddess grant us welfare,” “May the varaṇa ward off,” pippalī, vidradhasya, and yā babhrava constitute the group for <s>gaṇa</s> rites; it is also the healing group.

children.text: iti bhaiṣajyagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the healing group.

children.text: ayaṃ te yonir ā no bhara dhītī vā ya ity arthasūktam utthāpano gaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The hymns beginning “This is your womb,” “Bring it to us,” and the <s>Arthasūkta</s> beginning dhītī vā ya constitute the raising group.

children.text: ity utthāpanagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the raising group.

children.text: ambayo yanti śambhumayobhū hiraṇyavarṇā niḥsālāṃ ye agnayo brahma jajñānam ity ekaita devā mṛgārasūktāny uttamaṃ varjayitvāpa naḥ śośucad aghaṃ punantu mā sasruṣīr himavataḥ pra sravanti vāyog pūtaḥ pavitreṇa śaṃ ca no mayaś ca no 'naḍudbhyas tvaṃ mahyam āpo vaiśvānaro raśmibhir yamo mṛtyur viśvajit saṃjñānaṃ no yady antarikṣe punar maitv indriyaṃ śivā naḥ śaṃ no vāto vātu agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn iti śāntigaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The pacification group consists of the hymns beginning ambayo yanti, “For welfare and happiness,” hiraṇyavarṇāḥ, niḥsālām, ye agnayaḥ, brahma jajñānam, “These gods,” the <s>Mṛgāra</s> hymns with the last omitted, apa naḥ śośucad agham, punantu mā, sasruṣīḥ, “They flow forth from the <s>Himālaya</s>,” “Purified by <s>Vāyu</s> with the purifier,” “Both welfare and happiness for us,” anaḍudbhyaḥ, tvaṃ mahyam āpaḥ, vaiśvānaraḥ, raśmibhiḥ, yamo mṛtyuḥ, viśvajit, “Concord for us,” “Whatever is in the midspace,” “May my faculty return,” “Auspicious for us,” “May the wind blow welfare to us,” and “We address <s>Agni</s> and the forest trees.”

children.text: iti sarvaiḥ sūktaiḥ kauśikoktabṛhacchāntigaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With all these hymns, this is the great pacification group taught by <s>Kauśika</s>.

children.text: ambayo yanti śambhumayobhū hiraṇyavarṇā uta devā yady antarikṣe punar naitv indriyaṃ śivā naḥ śaṃ no vāto vātv agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn iti śāntātīyo laghuśāntigaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The light pacification group of the <s>Śāntātiya</s> consists of the hymns beginning ambayo yanti, “For welfare and happiness,” hiraṇyavarṇāḥ, “These gods,” “Whatever is in the midspace,” “May my faculty return,” “Auspicious for us,” “May the wind blow welfare to us,” and “We address <s>Agni</s> and the forest trees.”

children.text: ye triṣaptā mamāgne varcaḥ prātar agniṃ girāv aragarāṭeṣu divas pṛthivyā hastivarcasaṃ siṃhe vyāghre yaśo havir yas te gandha iti tisṛbhir varcasyagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The group for brilliance consists of the hymns beginning “Those three times seven,” “My brilliance, <s>Agni</s>,” “<s>Agni</s> in the morning,” girāv aragarāṭeṣu, “From heaven and earth,” “Elephant-like brilliance,” “In lion and tiger,” “The oblation of fame,” and the three verses beginning “That fragrance of yours.”

children.text: yā asurā manuṣyā mā no vidan namo devavadhebhya ity abhayagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hymns beginning “The <s>Asuras</s> and human beings who,” “May they not discover us,” and “Homage to the divine weapons” constitute the fearlessness group.

children.text: bhūto bhūteṣv iti rājānam abhiṣekagaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hymn beginning “Being among beings” constitutes the group for the consecration of a king.
